q1_issues.issue: `Goal` is the spatial 'to / into' destination oblique of a motion result; 'turned into rivers' names the resulting kind, so `Goal` asserts a displacement toward rivers that the sentence does not state.
A descriptive modifier on a definite plural ('the rapid currents') distributes over the members via the group plus distribution rule, rather than being predicated of the group symbol itself.

q2_gaps: copular-change 'turn into N' / 'become N': the resultatives section covers only a state result (reified state + flat atom + `Result`) and a motion result (`Source` / `Goal`), so a resulting predicate NOMINAL has no assigned form

the 'with + NP + past participle' absolute clause ('with vehicles swept away by the rapid currents'): it is neither a comitative PP (CoAgent / Instrument) nor one of the licensed connectives, so its dependence on the main clause has no representation

a bare plural subject in an EPISODIC PAST verbal clause ('Roads turned into rivers'): bare plurals are routed to the generic rule form, and group witnesses are specified for definite / counted plurals, leaving this case undecided (and with it, whether the distributive per-member rule is also owed)
notes: The phrasal verb kept whole as `sweep_away`, the passive by-phrase taking `Agent` on an inanimate, and `Theme` for the displaced-but-unchanged vehicles all follow the instruction set.
